_readme: Lineage graph. tier: chapter | profile | sidebar | node | root. kind: person | tradition | institution | symbolic. Edge type: initiated | lived-with | influenced | claimed | reacted-against | institutional | family | lineage | protected. evidence: documented | testimony | hagiographic | devotional. verified=true means checked against sources during chapter writing; everything else is a draft to verify.

nodes.name: Varkari tradition (Vithoba bhakti)
nodes.note: Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Tukaram

nodes.name: Rammohan Roy
nodes.note: Born 1772 (some sources 1774); Upanishad translations 1816–1819; founded the Brahmo Sabha, 20 August 1828; died Bristol 27 September 1833

nodes.name: Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.note: Arya Samaj founder; born Mul Shankar at Tankara; four Vedic Samhitas as sole self-evident revelation; not Swami Dayananda of Arsha Vidya

nodes.name: Debendranath Tagore
nodes.note: Born 15 May 1817, Jorasanko; Tattvabodhini Sabha 6 Oct 1839; Brahmo covenant 21 Dec 1843 (7 Pous 1765 Shaka); four students to Benares 1845; Vedic infallibility abandoned c. 1847-1850; Brahmo Dharma (1848-1854 in different sources); Adi Brahmo Samaj after 1866; Santiniketan lease 1863 (Visva-Bharati; 1867 in Banglapedia and Wikipedia); Anglo-Hindu College 1827 or 1829; died 19 Jan 1905

nodes.name: Keshab Chandra Sen
nodes.note: Born 19 Nov 1838, Calcutta; joined Brahmo Samaj 1857 (some say 1859); acharya 1862; Brahmo Samaj of India 11 or 15 Nov 1866; lecture on Jesus Christ May 1866; England 1870; Act III of 1872; Cooch Behar marriage 1878; Nava Vidhan Jan 1880 (1881 in some sources); died 8 Jan 1884

nodes.name: Jyotirao Phule
nodes.note: Mali caste, Poona; girls' school 1848; Gulamgiri June 1873; Satyashodhak Samaj 24 Sept 1873; one Creator (Nirmik) without mediators; titled Mahatma 11 May 1888; died 28 Nov 1890

nodes.name: Ramakrishna
nodes.note: Priest of the Dakshineswar Kali temple; 'as many faiths, so many paths'

nodes.name: Swami Vivekananda
nodes.note: Narendranath Datta. Ramakrishna's chief disciple; 1893 Parliament of Religions; four yogas and Practical Vedanta; founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1 May 1897).

nodes.name: Sree Narayana Guru
nodes.note: Birth year given as 1854, 1855 or 1856 in different sources; 1854 follows Britannica and Nataraja Guru's chronology.

nodes.name: Chandrasekharendra Saraswati
nodes.note: Swaminathan; the Kanchi Paramacharya, 68th head of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham from 13 February 1907 to his death on 8 January 1994. Orthodox counterpoint in Part 2: one God behind all religions, but no conversion and varna by birth. Talks compiled as Deivathin Kural (English: Hindu Dharma).

nodes.name: Sarada Devi
nodes.note: Saradamani Mukhopadhyay of Jayrambati; Ramakrishna's wife and first disciple; the Holy Mother; died 20 or 21 July 1920

nodes.name: Swami Rama Tirtha
nodes.note: Tirath Ram Goswami; Lahore mathematics teacher; lectured in Japan and the USA 1902–1904; died in the Ganga 17 October 1906

nodes.name: Chattampi Swamikal
nodes.note: Born Ayyappan (Kunjan), 25 August 1853; died Panmana, 5 May 1924.

nodes.name: S. Radhakrishnan
nodes.note: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan; born Tiruttani 5 September 1888; died Madras 17 April 1975; philosopher of intuition and religious experience

nodes.name: Swami Chinmayananda
nodes.note: Balakrishna Menon; born Ernakulam 8 May 1916; sannyasa from Sivananda 25 February 1949; Chinmaya Mission 1953; died San Diego 3 August 1993

nodes.name: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya)
nodes.note: Natarajan; born Manjakkudi 15 August 1930; sannyasa from Chinmayananda 1962; Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Saylorsburg, 1986; died Rishikesh 23 September 2015

nodes.name: Swami Sarvapriyananda
nodes.note: Biswarup Mitra; Ramakrishna Order (joined 1994); minister of the Vedanta Society of New York since January 2017

nodes.name: Acharya Prashant
nodes.note: Prashant Tripathi; reportedly born Agra, 1978; PrashantAdvait Foundation 2015; Vedanta online, mostly in Hindi

nodes.name: Totapuri
nodes.note: Naga monk of the Puri order, probably from the Punjab; gave Ramakrishna sannyasa, 1864 or 1865

nodes.name: Bhairavi Brahmani
nodes.note: Brahmin woman ascetic from Jessore; Tantric and Vaishnava teacher of Ramakrishna, 1861–1863

nodes.name: Arunachala (the hill as Shiva)
nodes.note: Named by Ramana as his guru

nodes.name: Bhausaheb Maharaj
nodes.note: Founded the Inchegiri line

nodes.name: Ramesh Balsekar
nodes.note: Translator and later teacher

nodes.name: Maurice Frydman
nodes.note: Editor and translator of I Am That

nodes.name: Swami Yogananda (of Calcutta)
nodes.note: Atmananda's guru; not Paramahansa Yogananda

nodes.name: Western Direct Path teachers
nodes.note: Jean Klein, Francis Lucille, Rupert Spira and others

nodes.name: Paul Brunton
nodes.note: British writer; popularizer

nodes.name: Western Neo-Advaita
nodes.note: Gangaji, Mooji, Eli Jaxon-Bear and others

nodes.name: Sri Aurobindo
nodes.note: Aurobindo Ghose; Cambridge classicist, Baroda teacher, Calcutta nationalist editor; Alipore bomb case 1908–09 (acquitted); Pondicherry from 4 April 1910; Integral Yoga, the Supermind, The Life Divine, Savitri

nodes.name: Rabindranath Tagore
nodes.note: Poet; son of Debendranath Tagore; Shilaidaha estates from 1890; Santiniketan school 1901; Visva-Bharati 1921; Gitanjali (1910, English 1912); Nobel 1913; The Religion of Man (Hibbert Lectures 1930, pub. 1931); jivan devata; Baul Man of the Heart

nodes.name: Muhammad Iqbal
nodes.note: Poet-philosopher of Sialkot and Lahore; Cambridge, Munich doctorate (1907/1908), Lincoln's Inn 1908; Asrar-i-Khudi 1915; knighted 1923 (New Year honours; 1922 in some sources); Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam (1930, 1934); khudi; Allahabad address Dec 1930

nodes.name: K. C. Bhattacharyya
nodes.note: Krishnachandra Bhattacharyya of Serampore; The Subject as Freedom (1930); 'Svaraj in Ideas' (Chandernagore, Oct 1931; pub. 1954); 'The Concept of Philosophy' (1936); death year 1947 in some sources; Amalner 1933-35; King George V professor, Calcutta, 1935-37

nodes.name: Gopi Krishna
nodes.note: Kashmiri Pandit; Public Works Department clerk; kundalini awakening Christmas season 1937 near Jammu; Kundalini: The Evolutionary Energy in Man (1967); kundalini as the biological mechanism of human evolution

nodes.name: Lahiri Mahasaya
nodes.note: Shyama Charan Lahiri, b. 30 Sept 1828 Ghurni, Nadia; d. 26 Sept 1895 Benares. Clerk/accountant, Military Engineering Department 1851-1886; Kriya Yoga for householders from 1861

nodes.name: Paramahansa Yogananda
nodes.note: Born Mukunda Lal Ghosh, Gorakhpur, 5 January 1893; died Los Angeles, 7 March 1952. Founded Yogoda Satsanga Society (1917) and Self-Realization Fellowship (counted from 1920, incorporated 1935); Autobiography of a Yogi (1946).

nodes.name: T. Krishnamacharya
nodes.note: Born Muchukundapura, 18 November 1888; died Madras, 28 February 1989.

nodes.name: Swami Sivananda
nodes.note: Kuppuswami, born Pattamadai 8 September 1887; doctor in Malaya c. 1913-1923; reached Rishikesh 1924 (DLS) or 1922 (Krishnananda); sannyasa from Vishvananda Saraswati, Rishikesh, 1 June 1924; Divine Life Society 1936; Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy 1948; Yoga of Synthesis; died Rishikesh 14 July 1963.

nodes.name: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi
nodes.note: Born Mahesh Prasad Varma (also Srivastava), 12 January 1917 or 1918 (c. 1911 in some accounts), Jabalpur in most accounts; died Vlodrop, Netherlands, 5 February 2008; cremated at the Sangam, Allahabad, 11 February 2008. Founder of Transcendental Meditation.

nodes.name: Sri Sri Ravi Shankar
nodes.note: Sudarshan Kriya; Art of Living Foundation (1981)

nodes.name: Sadhguru (Jaggi Vasudev)
nodes.note: Born Jagadish Vasudev, Mysore, 3 September 1957. Chamundi Hill experience 23 September 1982 (his account); Isha Foundation 1992 (1993 in some accounts); Isha Yoga Center 1994; Dhyanalinga 1999; Inner Engineering and Shambhavi Mahamudra Kriya; Adiyogi bust 2017

nodes.name: Mahavatar Babaji
nodes.note: Known only through the accounts of Lahiri Mahasaya, his disciples and Yogananda; met Lahiri near Ranikhet in 1861 by Lahiri's account

nodes.name: Swami Vishnudevananda
nodes.note: Born Kerala 31 December 1927; came to Sivananda 1947 after reading a leaflet; first hatha yoga teacher at the Forest Academy; left for the West 1957; first Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre, Montreal, 1959; died 9 November 1993.

nodes.name: Brahmananda Saraswati (Jyotirmath)
nodes.note: Born Rajaram Mishra near Ayodhya; birth year given as 1868, 1870 or 1871; sannyasa 1904; Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath from April 1941 until his death in 1953; called Guru Dev in the TM movement

nodes.name: Swami Lakshmanjoo
nodes.note: Born Lakshman Raina, Srinagar, 9 May 1907; died Noida, 27 September 1991.

nodes.name: Swami Muktananda
nodes.note: Born Krishna, 16 May 1908 (year sometimes questioned), near Mangalore; shaktipat from Bhagavan Nityananda 15 August 1947; founded Gurudev Siddha Peeth (Ganeshpuri) and the SYDA Foundation (1974); died Ganeshpuri 2 October 1982.

nodes.name: Bhagavan Nityananda
nodes.note: Avadhuta of Ganeshpuri, Maharashtra; died 8 August 1961. Birth year uncertain.

nodes.name: Gurumayi Chidvilasananda
nodes.note: Born Malti Shetty, 24 June 1955; Muktananda's English translator from 1975; sannyasa 26 April 1982; co-successor 3 May 1982; sole head of Siddha Yoga from 10 November 1985.

nodes.name: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada
nodes.note: Born Abhay Charan De, Calcutta, 1 September 1896; initiated by Bhaktisiddhanta 1933; sannyasa 1959; Jaladuta to Boston 1965; founded ISKCON, New York, July 1966; Bhagavad-gita As It Is (1968/1972); died Vrindavan 14 November 1977

nodes.name: Anandamayi Ma
nodes.note: Self-initiated (1922); no human guru; Shree Shree Anandamayee Sangha

nodes.name: Mata Amritanandamayi (Amma)
nodes.note: Born Sudhamani Idamannel, 27 September 1953, Parayakadavu, Alappad, Kollam district, Kerala; bhava darshan from 1975; Mata Amritanandamayi Math registered 6 May 1981; first world tour 1987; darshan by embrace; no human guru

nodes.name: Bhaktivinoda Thakura
nodes.note: Kedarnath Datta, b. 2 Sep 1838 Ula (Birnagar); deputy magistrate; d. 23 Jun 1914.

nodes.name: Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati
nodes.note: Bimala Prasad Datta, b. 6 Feb 1874 Puri; d. 1 Jan 1937 Calcutta.

nodes.name: Shastriji Maharaj (BAPS)
nodes.note: Profile centres on Shastriji Maharaj (1865-1951, founded BAPS 1907) and summarises the line to Pramukh Swami, who now has his own node. Id kept as shastriji-pramukh; name and death year corrected so the node does not span two lives.

nodes.name: Neem Karoli Baba
nodes.note: Birth year approximate (c. 1900); birthplace district disputed (Firozabad or Ambedkar Nagar). Died 11 Sep 1973, Vrindavan.

nodes.name: Premanand Maharaj
nodes.note: Radhavallabh devotee, Vrindavan

nodes.name: Gaur Gopal Das
nodes.note: ISKCON monk and speaker

nodes.name: Mahant Swami Maharaj
nodes.note: Keshavjivandas Swami, named successor 20 Jul 2012; guru of BAPS from 13 Aug 2016. Birth year per Wikipedia lineage list; verify.

nodes.name: Shirdi Sai Baba
nodes.note: Birth date and place unknown; Pathri claim disputed

nodes.name: Meher Baba
nodes.note: Merwan Sheriar Irani, b. 25 Feb 1894 Pune; silent from 10 July 1925; first publicly declared himself the Avatar Feb 1954 (Trust brief biography); Meher Baba's Call issued 12 Sept 1954 at a mass darshan in Ahmednagar; Final Declaration 30 Sept 1954 at Meherabad; d. 31 Jan 1969 Meherazad, entombed at Meherabad.

nodes.name: Upasni Maharaj
nodes.note: Kashinath Govind Upasni; b. 15 May 1870 Satana; d. 24 Dec 1941 Sakori. Settled at Sakori 1917, 1918 or 1922 depending on source; Meher Baba Trust chronology has Merwan visiting him at Sakori in 1916-17.

nodes.name: Hazrat Babajan
nodes.note: Pashtun faqir of Pune; birth estimates c. 1790-1820; d. 21 Sept 1931 Pune; kiss on Merwan's forehead dated May 1913 (embrace) / Jan 1914 (kiss) in Trust chronology.

nodes.name: Tajuddin Baba
nodes.note: Nagpur saint; b. 17 or 27 Jan 1861 depending on source; d. 17 Aug 1925.

nodes.name: Narayan Maharaj
nodes.note: Of Kedgaon; b. 20 May 1885, d. 3 Sept 1945 per Wikipedia; birthplace given as Nargund or Bagalkot.

nodes.name: Shiv Dayal Singh (Soamiji)
nodes.note: Founder of the Radhasoami faith; opened public satsang at Panni Gali, Agra, on Basant Panchami, 15 February 1861. Succession disputed between branches.

nodes.name: Inayat Khan
nodes.note: Born Baroda 5 July 1882; Chishti initiation under Abu Hashim Madani, Hyderabad, c. 1903-1904; sailed for the US 13 September 1910; Sufi Order in London (1914, 1915 or 1918 in different sources); Universal Worship, London, 1921 (Suluk Press); Sufi Movement, Geneva, 1923; died Delhi 5 February 1927

nodes.name: Ramalinga Swamigal (Vallalar)
nodes.note: Ramalingam; b. 5 Oct 1823 Marudur; vanished 30 Jan 1874 Mettukuppam by followers' account. Death is a faith claim.

nodes.name: Gurinder Singh Dhillon
nodes.note: Head of Radha Soami Satsang Beas

nodes.name: Kamlesh Patel (Daaji)
nodes.note: Current guide of Heartfulness

nodes.name: Mahatma Gandhi
nodes.note: Religious thought: Truth is God, ahimsa, satyagraha, the ashram vows, a nonviolent reading of the Gita.

nodes.name: S.N. Goenka
nodes.note: Born in Burma; outside the book's scope but on the tree

nodes.name: J. Krishnamurti
nodes.note: Born Madanapalle (11 May 1895 per Lutyens; claims range 4 May 1895 to 25 May 1896); dissolved the Order of the Star at Ommen, 3 August 1929; died Ojai, 17 February 1986.

nodes.name: U.G. Krishnamurti
nodes.note: b. 9 Jul 1918 Machilipatnam; d. 22 Mar 2007 Vallecrosia (memorial compilation gives 22 Mar 2.30 pm; Wikipedia cites The Hindu of 25 Mar 2007, the likely origin of the '25 March' date).

nodes.name: Baba Ramdev
nodes.note: Televised pranayama; Patanjali Ayurved. Birth year uncertain (1965-1975), so born is left blank

nodes.name: Nithyananda (Kailasa)
nodes.note: Declared the 'nation' of Kailasa after leaving India in 2019

nodes.name: Thycaud Ayyavu Swamikal
nodes.note: Tamil-born yogi in Thiruvananthapuram; taught hatha yoga to Chattampi Swamikal and Narayana Guru.

nodes.name: Kummampilli Raman Pillai Asan
nodes.note: Sanskrit scholar of central Travancore who taught Narayana Guru from about 1877.

nodes.name: Dr P. Palpu
nodes.note: Ezhava physician; organiser of the SNDP Yogam (1903); father of Nataraja Guru.

nodes.name: Kumaran Asan
nodes.note: Malayalam poet and disciple of Narayana Guru; first general secretary of the SNDP Yogam.

nodes.name: Nataraja Guru
nodes.note: Disciple of Narayana Guru; founded the Narayana Gurukula in 1923; commentator on his works.

nodes.name: Guru Nitya Chaitanya Yati
nodes.note: Disciple of Nataraja Guru; author of That Alone, a commentary on the Atmopadesa Satakam.

nodes.name: Neelakanta Theerthapada
nodes.note: Disciple of Chattampi Swamikal from 1893.

nodes.name: Theerthapada Paramahamsa
nodes.note: Disciple of Chattampi Swamikal from 1898.

nodes.name: Jatadhari
nodes.note: Wandering Vaishnava (Rama) monk; gave Ramakrishna the Ramlala image, c. 1864

nodes.name: Govinda Roy
nodes.note: Hindu convert to Islam on a Sufi path; instructed Ramakrishna in Islamic practice, 1866

nodes.name: Mahendranath Gupta ("M")
nodes.note: Schoolteacher; recorded the Kathamrita (Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna), 1882–1886

nodes.name: Christianity
nodes.note: Added for Ramakrishna's 1873/1874 Christian episode; merge with any existing Christianity root

nodes.name: Sister Nivedita (Margaret Noble)
nodes.note: Irish disciple of Vivekananda, initiated as a brahmacharini on 25 March 1898; author of The Master as I Saw Him (1910).

nodes.name: Sudhakar Chaturvedi
nodes.note: Vedic scholar associated with Gandhi; Sri Sri Ravi Shankar's first teacher

nodes.name: Swami Shankar Dev
nodes.note: Head of Kripalu Bagh Ashram, Kankhal; gave Ramdev sannyasa; missing since 14 July 2007

nodes.name: Acharya Karamveer
nodes.note: Arya Samaj yoga teacher; taught Ramdev yoga; co-founder of Divya Yog Mandir Trust (1995)

nodes.name: Acharya Balkrishna
nodes.note: Ramdev's partner; co-founder and managing director of Patanjali Ayurved

nodes.name: Swami Ram (Rama Joo) of Srinagar
nodes.note: Kashmiri Shaiva teacher and Lakshmanjoo's family guru; dates given as 1852–1914 (Lakshmanjoo Academy) or 1854–1915 (other sources).

nodes.name: Swami Mahatab Kak
nodes.note: Chief disciple of Swami Ram; initiated Lakshmanjoo and taught him the Shaiva scriptures.

nodes.name: Lilian Silburn
nodes.note: French Indologist; studied with Lakshmanjoo from 1948 and translated Kashmiri Shaiva texts into French.

nodes.name: Jaideva Singh
nodes.note: Indian scholar and musicologist; studied with Lakshmanjoo and translated the Shiva Sutras, Spanda Karikas and Vijnana Bhairava into English.

nodes.name: Alexis Sanderson
nodes.note: Oxford scholar of Shaivism; spent six years in Kashmir studying with Lakshmanjoo.

nodes.name: John Hughes
nodes.note: American student of Lakshmanjoo from 1971; recorded and edited his English teachings (Universal Shaiva Fellowship / Lakshmanjoo Academy).

nodes.name: Ramamohana Brahmachari
nodes.note: Himalayan yogi whom Krishnamacharya named as his teacher; no independent record has been found.

nodes.name: Indra Devi
nodes.note: Born Eugenie Peterson in Riga; studied with Krishnamacharya in Mysore in the late 1930s; taught yoga in Shanghai, Hollywood and Argentina.

nodes.name: Srivatsa Ramaswami
nodes.note: Long-time student of Krishnamacharya in Madras; teaches vinyasa krama.

nodes.name: A.G. Mohan
nodes.note: Student of Krishnamacharya in Madras; author of Krishnamacharya: His Life and Teachings (2010).

nodes.name: Hariharananda Tirthaswami (Nandakumar Vidyalankar)
nodes.note: Sanskrit scholar and Tantric teacher; taught Rammohan Sanskrit and, by biographers' accounts, initiated him into Tantric practice; stayed with him at Rangpur c. 1812

nodes.name: Ramchandra Vidyabagish
nodes.note: Sanskrit scholar and lexicographer; first secretary of the Brahmo Sabha (1828); kept services going after 1833; brought Debendranath Tagore into the Sabha's trust in 1843

nodes.name: Islamic theology and Persian learning
nodes.note: Rational and monotheist (tawhid) theology read in Arabic and Persian; shaped Rammohan's Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (c. 1804). Merge with any Islam root if one exists

nodes.name: Swami Virjananda (Virajanand Dandeesha)
nodes.note: Blind Sanskrit grammarian of Mathura; taught Dayananda c. 1860–1863; divided books into arsha (true) and anarsha (later, corrupt)

nodes.name: The Vedic Samhitas
nodes.note: The four collections of Vedic hymns and formulas (Rig, Yajur, Sama, Atharva); the only scripture Dayananda held self-authoritative

nodes.name: Swami Shraddhananda (Munshi Ram)
nodes.note: Arya Samaj leader; founded Gurukul Kangri (1902); led shuddhi campaign in the 1920s

nodes.name: Arya Samaj
nodes.note: Founded by Dayananda in Bombay, 10 April 1875; ten principles settled at Lahore, 1877

nodes.name: Mahadevendra Saraswati V
nodes.note: Born Lakshmikantan; 67th head of the Kanchi Kamakoti monastery for about a week (6-13 February 1907); maternal cousin of Chandrasekharendra Saraswati (Mahadevan). Samadhi at Kalavai.

nodes.name: Jayendra Saraswati
nodes.note: Born Subrahmanyam, 18 July 1935; given the name Jayendra Saraswati 22 March 1954; 69th head of the Kanchi monastery; arrested 11 November 2004 and charged with murder and criminal conspiracy in the Sankararaman case; acquitted with all co-accused by the Principal District and Sessions Court, Puducherry, 27 November 2013; no appeal filed; died 28 February 2018.

nodes.name: Bholanath (Ramani Mohan Chakravarti)
nodes.note: Anandamayi Ma's husband and first disciple; initiated by her at Bajitpur (Dec 1922 or 3 Jan 1923); died Kishenpur, Dehradun, 6 May 1938

nodes.name: Bhaiji (Jyotish Chandra Roy)
nodes.note: Dhaka devotee who named her Anandamayi (1925 per ashram chronology); died Almora, August 1937

nodes.name: Arnaud Desjardins
nodes.note: French writer and filmmaker; disciple of Anandamayi Ma

nodes.name: Mhalsapati
nodes.note: Khandoba temple priest at Shirdi who greeted the young fakir as 'Ya Sai'; lived closely with him

nodes.name: Abdul Baba
nodes.note: Muslim attendant of Shirdi Sai Baba from 1889; kept a notebook in Deccani Urdu (translated by Marianne Warren); caretaker of the tomb

nodes.name: Venkusa of Selu
nodes.note: Hindu guru named as Sai Baba's teacher in Das Ganu's Bhaktisaramrita (1925) and Narasimhaswami; claim only

nodes.name: B.V. Narasimhaswami
nodes.note: Promoter of Shirdi Sai Baba's worship from 1936; founded the All India Sai Samaj (1940); never met him

nodes.name: Swami Saradananda
nodes.note: Ramakrishna's disciple; Sarada Devi's guardian; built the Udbodhan house (she moved in 23 May 1909)

nodes.name: Swami Madhava Tirtha
nodes.note: Of the Dwarka Math; inspired Tirath Ram's study of Vedanta in Lahore

nodes.name: Puran Singh
nodes.note: Punjabi poet (17 Feb 1881 – 31 Mar 1931); met Rama Tirtha in Tokyo, September 1902; his biographer and editor

nodes.name: Tulsi Sahib of Hathras
nodes.note: Sant poet, author of Ghat Ramayan; teacher of Shiv Dayal Singh's parents, stayed in their house in Panni Gali, Agra. No record that he initiated Shiv Dayal Singh.

nodes.name: Salig Ram (Huzur Maharaj)
nodes.note: Postal official, Postmaster-General of the North-Western Provinces from 1881; met Shiv Dayal Singh 1858; asked for the public satsang of 1861; gave the faith the name Radhasoami; head of the main Agra group 1878-1898.

nodes.name: Vishnu Bhaskar Lele
nodes.note: Maharashtrian yogi; taught Aurobindo to silence the mind in three days of meditation in Baroda, January 1908

nodes.name: Mirra Alfassa (the Mother)
nodes.note: Born Paris 21 Feb 1878; met Aurobindo 29 March 1914; in Pondicherry from 24 April 1920; led the Sri Aurobindo Ashram from November 1926; founded Auroville 1968; died 17 Nov 1973

nodes.name: Auroville
nodes.note: International township near Pondicherry founded by the Mother; inaugurated 28 Feb 1968; Auroville Foundation Act 1988

nodes.name: Annie Besant
nodes.note: President of the Theosophical Society from 1907; Krishnamurti's guardian from 1910; head of the Order of the Star's sponsors.

nodes.name: C.W. Leadbeater
nodes.note: Theosophist and former Anglican curate who claimed clairvoyance; picked out Krishnamurti at Adyar in 1909 and called him Alcyone.

nodes.name: David Bohm
nodes.note: Physicist; read The First and Last Freedom c. 1959, met Krishnamurti c. 1960-61, recorded dialogues 1965-1984 (The Ending of Time, 1985).

nodes.name: Aldous Huxley
nodes.note: Novelist; met Krishnamurti in 1938 and became a close friend; encouraged and introduced The First and Last Freedom (1954).

nodes.name: Akshay Kumar Datta
nodes.note: Rationalist writer; edited the Tattvabodhini Patrika from 1843; led the radical Brahmos who pressed Debendranath to abandon Vedic infallibility (c. 1847-1850). Birth/death years from general knowledge, not rechecked this batch

nodes.name: Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
nodes.note: Founded 15 May 1878 by Sivanath Sastri, Ananda Mohan Bose and others who left Keshab after the Cooch Behar marriage; constitution with adult franchise

nodes.name: Thomas Paine
nodes.note: English-born radical; Phule read Rights of Man in 1847 and named Paine as an influence

nodes.name: A. G. Hogg
nodes.note: Scottish Presbyterian missionary and philosopher at Madras Christian College; supervised Radhakrishnan's MA thesis (1908)

nodes.name: Swami Tapovan Maharaj
nodes.note: Born Subrahmanyan Nair in Kerala, 3 December 1889; died 16 January 1957; taught Chinmayananda at Uttarkashi, 1949 onward

nodes.name: Swami Pranavananda (Gudivada)
nodes.note: Taught Dayananda of Arsha Vidya at Gudivada, Andhra Pradesh, in 1961; credited with his view of the Veda as pramana

nodes.name: Swami Tejomayananda
nodes.note: Disciple of Chinmayananda (sannyasa 21 October 1983); head of Chinmaya Mission 1993-2017

nodes.name: Swami Paramarthananda
nodes.note: Direct sannyasi disciple of Dayananda of Arsha Vidya; teaches in Chennai

nodes.name: Anantanand Rambachan
nodes.note: Trinidad-born scholar of Hinduism; studied under Dayananda at Sandeepany from 1973; author of The Limits of Scripture (1994)

nodes.name: Baul tradition
nodes.note: Wandering singers of rural Bengal from Hindu and Muslim backgrounds; songs of the moner manush (Man of the Heart); Lalon Fakir (d. 1890)

nodes.name: Thomas Arnold
nodes.note: British orientalist; Iqbal's teacher at Government College, Lahore, in the 1890s

nodes.name: Kalidas Bhattacharyya
nodes.note: Philosopher; son of K. C. Bhattacharyya

nodes.name: Panchanan Bhattacharya
nodes.note: Disciple of Lahiri Mahasaya; first authorised to initiate others; founded the Arya Mission Institution, Calcutta, c. 1885 or 1886

nodes.name: Keshavananda Brahmachari (Keshabananda)
nodes.note: Kriya disciple of Lahiri Mahasaya; ashram (Katyayani Peeth) at Vrindavan. Wikipedia gives 1830-1942; dates rest on devotional sources, so omitted

nodes.name: Rajaratna Manikrao
nodes.note: Founder of the Jummadada Vyayam Mandir, Baroda; trained Kuvalayananda in physical culture 1907-1910.

nodes.name: Paramahamsa Madhavdas
nodes.note: Yogi settled at Malsar near Baroda; Kuvalayananda's teacher from 1918/1919. Dates 1798-1921 given by Kaivalyadhama are unsourced, so omitted.

nodes.name: Seer Paranjyothi
nodes.note: Said to have initiated Vethathiri into kundalini yoga; known only from the movement's account.

nodes.name: Rajarsi Janakananda (James J. Lynn)
nodes.note: Kansas City businessman; gave Yogananda the Encinitas hermitage; SRF president 1952-1955

nodes.name: Daya Mata
nodes.note: Disciple of Yogananda; president of SRF/YSS 1955-2010

nodes.name: Swami Kriyananda (J. Donald Walters)
nodes.note: Disciple from 1948; asked to resign from SRF in 1962; founded Ananda near Nevada City, California, in 1968

nodes.name: Nigamananda Paramahansa
nodes.note: Bengali Tantric and Advaita teacher; his tradition says Bamakhepa initiated him. Born Nalinikanta Chattopadhyay, 18 Aug 1880; died Calcutta 29 Nov 1935 (Wikipedia).

nodes.name: Kailashpati Baba
nodes.note: Tantric teacher at Tarapith, first guru of Bamakhepa in devotional biographies. No dates; known only from those accounts.

nodes.name: Mokshadananda
nodes.note: Second teacher of Bamakhepa in devotional biographies (also Mokshananda, Mokshadanandanath). No dates; known only from those accounts.

nodes.name: Ram Dass
nodes.note: Born Richard Alpert, Boston, 6 Apr 1931; met Neem Karoli Baba 1967; Be Here Now (1971); died Maui 22 Dec 2019.

nodes.name: Mataji Krishnabai
nodes.note: Disciple of Papa Ramdas; co-founder and later head of Anandashram until 1989.

nodes.name: Swami Satchidananda (Anandashram)
nodes.note: Joined Anandashram 1949; led it after Krishnabai until 2008. Not the Integral Yoga founder of the same name.

nodes.name: Siddharudha Swami of Hubli
nodes.note: Hubli saint who advised Ramdas in 1923. Dates not verified, omitted.

nodes.name: Swami Vishvananda Saraswati
nodes.note: Dashanami (Saraswati) monk who gave Kuppuswami sannyasa and the name Sivananda at Rishikesh on 1 June 1924; by Krishnananda's account they met only briefly. Dates unknown.

nodes.name: Swami Chidananda
nodes.note: Sridhar Rao, born 24 September 1916; joined Sivananda 1943; sannyasa 10 July 1949; general secretary of the Divine Life Society from late 1948; president from August 1963; died 28 August 2008.

nodes.name: Swami Krishnananda
nodes.note: Subbaraya, born 25 April 1922; came to Sivananda 1944; sannyasa 14 January 1946; secretary for finance from 1957; general secretary of the Divine Life Society from 1961 until his death on 23 November 2001.

nodes.name: Swami Satchidananda
nodes.note: C. K. Ramaswamy, born 22 December 1914 near Coimbatore; sannyasa from Sivananda 1949; Integral Yoga in the US; opening address at Woodstock, August 1969; died Chennai 19 August 2002.

nodes.name: Swami Sivananda Radha
nodes.note: Ursula Sylvia Hellman, born Berlin 20 March 1911; sannyasa from Sivananda 1956; Yasodhara Ashram, Kootenay Bay, British Columbia (from 1963); died 30 November 1995.

nodes.name: Swami Venkatesananda
nodes.note: Disciple and biographer of Sivananda (Sivananda: Biography of a Modern Sage); later taught in South Africa and Australia (Fremantle).

nodes.name: Deepak Chopra
nodes.note: Endocrinologist; met Maharishi 1985, directed the movement's Ayurvedic centre at Lancaster, Massachusetts, promoted Maharishi Ayur-Veda; parted from the movement in the early 1990s

nodes.name: Tony Nader (Maharaja Adhiraj Rajaraam)
nodes.note: Physician and neuroscientist; named head of the Global Country of World Peace (2000); leads the TM organisations after Maharishi's death in 2008

nodes.name: Malladihalli Raghavendra Swami (Tiruka)
nodes.note: Yoga teacher; Anatha Sevashrama Trust, Malladihalli, Chitradurga district, Karnataka; wrote on Suryanamaskara; taught hatha yoga to the boy Jaggi Vasudev

nodes.name: Palani Swami (guru of a previous life, by Sadhguru's account)
nodes.note: Named, in accounts drawing on Arundhathi Subramaniam's authorised biography (name not seen in the book itself by the checker), as the guru of Sadhguru's earlier life as Shivayogi; no independent historical record

nodes.name: Gunatitanand Swami
nodes.note: Mulji Jani, b. Bhadra; initiated by Swaminarayan 1810 at Dabhan; mahant of Junagadh for 40 years; d. 11 Oct 1867 Gondal. BAPS holds he was the earthly form of Akshar; Vadtal and Ahmedabad leadership reject this. Birth 28 Sep 1784 (Wikipedia) or 1785 in other sources.

nodes.name: Bhagatji Maharaj
nodes.note: Pragji Bhakta, tailor of Mahuva, b. 20 Mar 1829; taught Akshar-Purushottam; Shastriji's guru. Death 7 Nov 1897 or 1898 (Wikipedia is inconsistent).

nodes.name: Yogiji Maharaj
nodes.note: Jina Vasani, b. 23 May 1892 Dhari; swami initiation 11 Apr 1911 (Gnanjivandas); met Shastriji at Rajkot 12 Aug 1910; BAPS guru 1951-1971; d. 23 Jan 1971 Mumbai.

nodes.name: Pramukh Swami Maharaj
nodes.note: Shantilal Patel, b. 7 Dec 1921 Chansad; parshad 22 Nov 1939 Ahmedabad, swami 10 Jan 1940 Gondal; BAPS president from 21 May 1950, guru 1971-2016; d. 13 Aug 2016 Sarangpur.

nodes.name: Bipin Bihari Goswami
nodes.note: Hereditary guru of the Baghnapara family who initiated Bhaktivinoda (1880 per Wikipedia). Dates unknown.

nodes.name: Jagannath Das Babaji
nodes.note: Vrindavan Vaishnava ascetic; instructing guru of Bhaktivinoda in Gaudiya Math tradition, disputed by other descendants. Dates not verified.

nodes.name: Gaura Kishora Dasa Babaji
nodes.note: Renunciant who initiated Bhaktisiddhanta (1900 or 1901). Dates not verified.

nodes.name: Zipruanna
nodes.note: Avadhuta of Maharashtra; by accounts drawing on Muktananda's own telling, sent him back to Nityananda. Dates not verified.

nodes.name: Swami Nityananda (Shanti Mandir)
nodes.note: Born Subhash Shetty; named Muktananda's successor July 1981 at South Fallsburg; co-head of Siddha Yoga with his sister from 3 May 1982; announced his withdrawal 3 November 1985; founded Shanti Mandir (1987 in most sources). Not to be confused with Bhagavan Nityananda of Ganeshpuri.

nodes.name: Bhakti Prajnana Keshava
nodes.note: Disciple of Bhaktisiddhanta; founder of the Gaudiya Vedanta Samiti; gave sannyasa to A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami at the Keshavji Gaudiya Math, Mathura, 17 September 1959

nodes.name: Bhaktivedanta Narayana Maharaja
nodes.note: Disciple of Bhakti Prajnana Keshava; by his followers' account performed Prabhupada's burial rites in 1977; many Western ISKCON members joined him in the 1990s; the GBC has disputed the closeness he claimed to Prabhupada

nodes.name: George Harrison
nodes.note: Beatle; produced the 1969 Hare Krishna mantra single by the London Radha Krishna Temple; bought Bhaktivedanta Manor for the movement in 1973

nodes.name: Swami Amritaswarupananda Puri
nodes.note: Amma's senior-most disciple; met her in 1979 aged 22; sannyasa 1989; vice-chairman of the Mata Amritanandamayi Math and president of Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; author of the movement's biography of Amma

nodes.name: Godavari Mataji
nodes.note: Sati Godavari Mataji of Sakori; arrived 1924 aged 10; named Upasni's successor (Hinduism Today); led the Kanya Kumari Sthan after 1941. Dates 1914-1990 from Wikipedia and a Cafoscari interview title; Hinduism Today gives none.

nodes.name: Zoroastrian tradition
nodes.note: Family background of Meher Baba; Zoroaster is the first of the six earlier Avatars in his scheme.

nodes.name: Sufism Reoriented
nodes.note: California Sufi group accepted Meher Baba as its leader and renamed by him in 1952; publishes God Speaks and God in a Pill?

nodes.name: Pete Townshend
nodes.note: Guitarist of The Who; heard of Meher Baba from Mike McInnerney in autumn 1967 (his account, Rolling Stone 1970); dedicated Tommy (1969) to him.

nodes.name: Sayyid Muhammad Abu Hashim Madani
nodes.note: Hyderabad Sufi teacher, head of the Chishti-Nizami-Kalimi line; Inayat Khan's murshid. Death given as 1907 (Wikipedia) or 1908 (Inayati Order)

nodes.name: Maulabakhsh (Sholay Khan)
nodes.note: Baroda musician and notation pioneer; founded the Gayanshala in 1886; Inayat Khan's maternal grandfather

nodes.name: Rabia Martin (Ada Martin)
nodes.note: First American disciple of Inayat Khan (San Francisco, 1910 or 1911); broke away after 1927; her line led to Sufism Reoriented

nodes.name: Maheboob Khan
nodes.note: Inayat Khan's brother; led the Sufi Movement from 1927 until his death in 1948; a council voted by majority to appoint him esoteric leader (Sufipedia chronology, 14-15 June, year not shown); followed by Mohammed Ali Khan (1948-1958) and Musharaff Khan (to 1967)

nodes.name: Vilayat Inayat Khan
nodes.note: Inayat Khan's eldest son; designated successor by his father in 1926; took up his father's mantle in 1956 or 1957 outside the Sufi Movement; revived the name Sufi Order in 1968 (now the Inayati Order / Inayatiyya); died 17 June 2004

nodes.name: Zia Inayat Khan
nodes.note: Vilayat's son; invested 2000; leads the Inayati Order (Inayatiyya)

nodes.name: Noor Inayat Khan
nodes.note: Inayat Khan's eldest daughter; SOE wireless operator; shot at Dachau 13 September 1944
